candidates.decision_relevance: Point-in-time hourly BTC, ETH, ETH/BTC, funding, open interest, and price sequences would establish whether deterioration preceded recovery or merely followed it, reducing sequence-error and hindsight-leakage uncertainty.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped hourly price, relative-performance, funding, and open-interest sequence
candidates.missing_history_problem: The reviews repeatedly use completed-week paths and asynchronous endpoint observations, but no common timestamped intrawweek history or point-in-time cutoff reconstruction is supplied.

candidates.decision_relevance: A stable-universe breadth history would test whether the reported 21%, 29%, 69%, and 78% readings represented persistent participation deterioration or changing-membership endpoint noise.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped fixed-universe breadth and participation series
candidates.missing_history_problem: Available breadth is explicitly a point-in-time top-100 proxy with changing membership; its construction, universe, and intraperiod path are unavailable, so broad rotation and distribution interpretations cannot be separated.

candidates.decision_relevance: Complete, timestamped liquidation, venue-level order-flow, depth, and positioning events would distinguish deleveraging or a transient stress event from persistent liquidity deterioration and identify lead-lag relationships with price weakness.
candidates.metric_name: Complete venue-covered liquidation, order-flow, depth, and positioning event history
candidates.missing_history_problem: Liquidations are lower-bound, fragile legacy aggregates; OI and microstructure observations lack full venue, instrument, magnitude, and timing detail, preventing assessment of whether leverage changes led or followed price weakness.

candidates.decision_relevance: A continuous settled ETF-flow history aligned to the observation windows would test whether positive ETH flows persisted, were concentrated, or translated into price and participation support.
candidates.metric_name: Settled asset-level ETF flow and breadth sequence
candidates.missing_history_problem: The required settled ETF sequence is unavailable or stale; current claims rely on isolated settled totals or proxy breadth, leaving flow persistence and within-week sequencing untestable.

candidates.decision_relevance: Frozen candidate snapshots, issue times, horizons, bounds, and matured outcomes would permit direct audit of ex-ante availability, range containment, false positives, false negatives, and warning opportunity cost.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Candidate counts are reported but objects, issue timestamps, cutoffs, target specifications, and matured outcomes are absent; the exit-calibration sidecar has zero matured rows and cannot quantify calibration or opportunity cost.

candidates.decision_relevance: Timestamp-aligned macro and liquidity-sensitive market data would provide missing context for distinguishing crypto-specific leverage stress from broader financial-conditions deterioration.
candidates.metric_name: Historical macro and financial-conditions observation sequence
candidates.missing_history_problem: Macro data are repeatedly unavailable, so the analyses cannot determine whether price, breadth, and leverage changes occurred alongside or independently of broader financial-conditions shifts.

candidates.decision_relevance: Historical stablecoin supply, exchange-transfer, and market-liquidity observations would test whether nominal stablecoin growth translated into deployable liquidity during the conflicting rotation and pullback episodes.
candidates.missing_history_problem: The supplied material treats stablecoin data as supply context only and does not provide a historical transmission or deployment sequence, leaving liquidity support versus withdrawal unresolved.
